caveats: **DISM is process-global and single-session.** The DISM API cannot safely run concurrent sessions from one process, so every `list` or `info` call is serialised through agent-core's `DismSlot`. A second caller receives `windows:dism:busy` rather than risking undefined behaviour, and a call rejected by the bounded-call outstanding-call ceiling is reported the same way.

**A timed-out call is `abandoned`, not cleared, until the worker returns.** If `DismGetFeatures` or `DismGetFeatureInfo` exceeds the 17 second limit, the dispatching thread reports `windows:dism:timeout` and marks the slot abandoned. Every later call reports `windows:dism:abandoned` until the original worker finishes, which is permanent if DISM itself never returns and is cleared only by a service restart.

**Pending states come from the feature enum, not a reboot-pending registry key.** `pending_enable` and `pending_disable` reflect DISM's `InstallPending` and `UninstallPending` values, and `list` sets `restart_required` to 1 only for those two states. `info` reports DISM's own `restart_type`, so an enabled feature can show `restart_required` 0 on `list` and `possible` on `info`.

**Feature names are DISM's internal names, and `disabled` covers three states.** `NetFx3`, `SMB1Protocol` and `TelnetClient` are the `FeatureName` values DISM uses, not Control Panel labels; `info` carries the operator-visible `display_name`. The `disabled` state also covers features whose payload is staged or removed, which the plugin does not tell apart.

**The macOS and Linux rows are placeholders by design.** DISM has no equivalent on either platform, so both legs return the `unsupported` row unconditionally, never an empty read or a fabricated value.

definitions.description: Detail for one Windows optional OS feature (DismGetFeatureInfo): its display name, description, state, and restart requirement. `feature` is bounded and character-restricted (`^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,256}$`) before it ever reaches DISM — an invalid value is refused with no DISM call. Windows-only: DISM has no Linux/macOS equivalent.

Enumerates Windows optional OS features (DismGetFeatures) and reports each one's state — enabled, disabled, pending_enable, pending_disable, superseded, partially_installed, or unknown — plus whether a restart is required to complete a pending change. An optional `state` filter narrows to one bucket (enabled = installed only; disabled = not present/removed/staged; pending = install/uninstall pending). Windows-only: DISM has no Linux/macOS equivalent.

description: Windows optional OS feature state (enabled/disabled/pending) via the DISM API
how_it_works:
The plugin reads which optional Windows features (Telnet client, TFTP, the IIS web server role, Virtual Machine Platform, .NET 3.5 and so on) are enabled, disabled or waiting on a restart, and changes nothing. `list` returns every feature with its state, optionally narrowed by a `state` filter; `info` returns one named feature with its display name, description and restart requirement. Both go through the Windows servicing API (DISM) in-process: no `dism.exe`, no WMI, no PowerShell.

Each call runs the same lifecycle on a worker thread: take the agent's single DISM slot, `DismInitialize`, `DismOpenSession` on the running OS, `DismGetFeatures` (`list`) or `DismGetFeatureInfo` (`info`), map each state number to a name, `DismCloseSession`, `DismShutdown`, release the slot. The whole call is bounded to 17 seconds. `DismApi.dll` is never linked; its eight exports are resolved from `System32` on first use. The slot, the session and the timeout all live in agent-core, which is never unloaded, so a worker that outlives a timeout never runs code belonging to a plugin that has been unloaded. Only one DISM call can be in flight in the agent at a time.

What it is not: no enable, disable, add, remove or commit (the eight resolved exports are the plugin's whole DISM surface and none of them mutates), no `dism.exe` subprocess, and no use of `Win32_OptionalFeature`.

outputs_note: Pipe-delimited rows via `write_output()`. `list` writes one `feature|` row per feature (or per matching feature when `state` filters; an unrecognised filter value is treated as no filter); `info` writes exactly one `feature_info|` row. An invalid `feature` value is refused before any DISM call with `feature_info|invalid|invalid 'feature' parameter: '<value>'` and exit code 1. On `list`, `restart_required` is 1 only for `pending_enable` and `pending_disable`; `info` reports DISM's own restart type. On an unsupported or unavailable leg, both actions instead write a single sentinel row: `feature|unsupported|<os>:dism:unsupported` / `feature|unavailable|windows:dism:<token>` (or the `feature_info` equivalent for `info`) — never a blank or omitted row.

result_status.when: a clean `list`/`info` read — the DISM call succeeded and the feature row(s) were written
`DismApi.dll` or one of its eight required exports could not be resolved from `System32`
Linux/macOS: DISM has no equivalent on this platform
`info`: the named feature does not exist (`DismGetFeatureInfo` returns `DISMAPI_E_UNKNOWN_FEATURE`)
another DISM call already holds the plugin's in-process slot, or the bounded-call outstanding-call ceiling rejected this call before it started
a previous call timed out and its worker has not returned; the DISM API is still held by that worker until it does
`DismGetFeatures`/`DismGetFeatureInfo` did not return within the 17s bounded timeout
a DISM session-lifecycle call failed with a non-access-denied HRESULT
an unhandled exception was caught inside the bounded DISM call
a DISM call in the session returned `E_ACCESSDENIED` — the caller's token lacks the elevated privilege the DISM API requires

where_the_data_goes: **Instruction result AND daily-sync inventory.** Rows travel over the agent's mTLS gRPC channel as the command response and land in the ResponseStore (`response_retention_days`, default 90 days), queryable at `/api/responses/{id}` and aggregatable (`list` groups by `state`, counted).

**Also consumed by** the `installed_software` daily-sync source (`agents/core/src/sync_source_installed_software.cpp`), which calls `list` in-process on the agent's 24 h schedule: every feature becomes a `feat` row with ecosystem `optional_feature` and its DISM state in `version`. Not consumed by the TAR warehouse, DEX, or metrics. `gather.ttlSeconds: 300` only caps how often a repeat dispatch is served from cache.

**Sensitivity.** Rows name which built-in Windows OS features are enabled on the device (e.g. `SMB1Protocol`, `TelnetClient`) — a security-relevant configuration signal, but no username, hostname, serial number or file path appears in any field.

**Siblings:** `msi_packages` (installed third-party/MSI software, not OS features), `windows_updates` (patch history, not feature toggles), `registry`/`wmi` (general-purpose Windows reads this plugin's narrow DISM surface deliberately does not replace) — none join with this plugin's output.

**MCP / REST.** Discover: `discover_plugins` (summary) → `yuzu://plugin-docs` (this page as data) → `discover_instructions` / `get_definition("windows.features.list")`. Run: `execute_instruction {definition_id, parameters}`. Read: `/api/responses/{id}`.
